title: Tommy Ladnier, Natty Dominique and Jimmy Noone
summary: He gives impressions of the tone and style of Ladnier, Dominique and Noone from the old Chicago days.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Is there anything more about, oh, one other fellow while I think of it, Tommy Ladner. I know you once mentioned him years ago. Oh, yes.

Yes. Tommy was sort of on the style of Joe Oliver's playing. Very similar. In fact, when Louie went to New York with Fletcher Henderson, Tommy Ladner took his place with Joe. And Tommy Ladner, because he could really blow. I heard him in the late years.

He was good even 19, oh, 38 and 39, right before he died I heard him. In those days, I remember some old Paramount ads and they called him the praying trumpet. Did he use a lot of that mute feature, that mute style or anything or sort of like, say, you'd plunge your style or anything. Was he specializing in that those days?
Yeah, he sort of got that from Joe.
How was his tone? Was it as big as Joe or?
Yeah, just not as big as Joe, but it was a good tone.
A big full tone.
Good sound.
Good sound. Do you remember where he played or anything about where you heard him? No. Except you say he played with Joe later, but I wondered any place else.
Gosh, I can't remember. It was someplace on the South Side I used to hear him play. Or I used to drift around different places.
Oh, I suppose you're all in it, yeah.
Mm-hmm. You're asking me to go way back now, you know, a little baby. That's kind of tough.

Another trumpet player I mentioned briefly, the last time I heard you in Chicago, Natty Dominic and I went up there at the Blue Note to hear that. Yes, I remember that. And I know you all had been friends for years. Did you hear him in the old days? Oh, yes.
Like, early, too? Mm-hmm. Dominic was good. He was all right.

I liked his tone. The last few years I heard him better on the old records. It sounds a little bit tweezy, you know, and sort of like a kazoo, you know, that metallic tone due to his mute or something. Yes. But how was his tone in person? You can't judge a fellow fairly by record. How did he sound when you first heard him? Was it a good full tone or sort of that metallic tone? What did you say?
It was a pretty good tone. Good tone, too, then. Not the tone that Joe got or Louie.
No one gets not, then.
Who can?
Yeah, that's right. Any other musicians? What about Jimmy Noon? Can you remember any impressions of him in the early days?
Oh, yes. He was a wonderful clarinet player. He really got a big sound. He could really execute around that horn.
I heard him a couple times, too, yeah.
And he could really swing. Gosh. It was really wonderful. Those days were all gone, though. Yeah, I'm afraid so.
All those fellas that died, no, 10 to 20 years ago so fast there, before we knew it, they were all gone.
